title: In 1984, Soviet cosmonaut Oleg Atkov flew a portable ultrasound to Salyut 7 and became the first doctor to image a human heart shrinking in real time in orbit
desc: In 1984, Soviet cardiologist Oleg Atkov spent 237 days aboard Salyut 7 with a portable echocardiography unit, producing what appear to be the first real-time ultrasound images of a human heart remodeling in microgravity — and founding a tradition of orbital imaging that still guides ISS medicine today.
